title: Outlook mobile: Purview DLP wait-on-send for iOS and Android
summary: Hold: the desktop comparison implies that every configured timeout eventually permits sending without evaluation, but the documented default of 9999 prevents that override. The roadmap facts and the qualified control rows are supported; two differences between Microsoft's reference pages should also be acknowledged.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans Purview DLP wait-on-send support for Outlook for iOS and Android.
claims.quote: Outlook for iOS and Android will support Microsoft Purview Data Loss Prevention (DLP) wait-on-send policies.

claims.claim: The planned capability lets organisations require DLP evaluation before sending an email.
claims.quote: Organizations can require a DLP evaluation before an email is sent

claims.claim: Organisations will be able to configure the wait for policy evaluation.
claims.quote: configure how long users must wait for policy evaluation to complete.

claims.claim: The new Outlook reference says its wait-to-send experience is controlled solely through the two Exchange parameters.
claims.quote: The wait‑to‑send experience is controlled solely through the following Exchange mailbox parameters:

claims.claim: DLPWaitOnSendEnabled defaults to false for new Outlook and enables presend evaluation when true.
claims.quote: **DLPWaitOnSendEnabled***boolean*: true or false.**Default**: false When true, it enables evaluation of the mail for Data loss prevention before mail is sent.

claims.claim: The new Outlook page gives a DLPWaitOnSendTimeout range of 0 to 10,000 seconds.
claims.quote: **DLPWaitOnSendTimeout***Integer*: range 0–10,000 seconds.
claims.fix: After the range, add: 'The Set-OrganizationConfig reference instead gives a valid range of 0 to 9999 seconds.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/exchangepowershell/set-organizationconfig#-dlpwaitonsendtimeout.

claims.claim: The new Outlook timeout default is 9999 seconds.
claims.quote: A valid value is an integer from 0 to 9999. The default value is 9999.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: A configured new Outlook timeout offers an override once it passes, without a qualification for 9999 or higher.
claims.quote: When DLPWaitOnSendTimeout >= 9999, user will never be allowed to send the email without DLP evaluation getting completed.
claims.fix: Replace the override explanation in What's changing and the corresponding Data exposure sentence with: 'For new Outlook, a timeout of 1 to 9998 seconds permits an override after that wait; 0 shows Send Anyway immediately; 9999 prevents sending until evaluation completes.' The parameter reference states these cases at https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/exchangepowershell/set-organizationconfig#-dlpwaitonsendtimeout. Keep the existing statement that mobile behaviour is not documented.

claims.claim: The desktop oversharing guide says evaluation duration can vary with internet speed, content length and policy count.
claims.quote: The duration for completing the evaluation can vary depending on factors such as internet speed, content length, and the number of policies defined.
